newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Danone aims to lead all sectors.
newsitem.headline: France's Danone aims to lead all sectors.

text.p: Food group Groupe Danone expects a rise in sales and improved results this year, despite a difficult start caused by new billing regulations, chairman Franck Riboud told the shareholders annual meeting Wednesday.
Although sales in the first quarter fell 0.9 percent on a like-for-like basis, the trend reversed last month and they were up 1.2 percent for the January-April period, he said.
The group aims to be leader in all its segments.
"We'll go alone, or keep making acquisitions, or we'll seek alliances to build partnerships...but we'll be No 1," Riboud said.
The planned merger of Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc did not affect Danone's strategy, he said, adding that the groups' activities were quite different.
Danone is the leading food group in France and the third in Europe. It is the world's biggest seller of mineral water.

It aims to double sales outside France to 30 billion francs by 2000. Last year, they represented 18 percent of the total, up from 14 percent. Danone's priority zones are Latin America, Asia and central Europe. It aims to double "Danone" brand sales in the next five years from the current 23 billion through internal growth and acquisitions.

Riboud said the packaging business was profitable and rich in cashflow, but was "not at the heart of Danone's strategy." The packaging business, the object of asset sale rumours, generates 92 percent of its six billion francs of sales in the food business.
But Danone will not sell its Kronenbourg beer business.
"We don't have any desire to sell Kronenbourg," he said.
